name: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease, Fitz-Hugh-Curtis Syndrome and Vaginitis

reference.source: Gynaecology by Ten Teachers 21st Edition / CDC STI Treatment Guidelines
clinicalPearls: Cervical motion tenderness chandelier sign and adnexal tenderness form primary clinical criteria for PID
CDC outpatient regimen is intramuscular Ceftriaxone 500 mg plus oral Doxycycline and Metronidazole for fourteen days
Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome represents perihepatic inflammation with violin-string adhesions between liver capsule and diaphragm
Bacterial vaginosis is diagnosed by Amsel criteria requiring clue cells, whiff test positivity, and pH above 4.5
Trichomoniasis features strawberry cervix and motile flagellated protozoa on wet mount, requiring partner treatment
reference.pathophysiology: Pelvic inflammatory disease results from ascending polymicrobial infection from the lower genital tract through the endocervix into endometrium, fallopian tubes, and pelvic peritoneum. Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae breach the endocervical barrier, initiating purulent salpingitis, epithelial deciliation, and tubal scarring that predisposes to ectopic pregnancy and chronic pelvic pain. Vaginitis stems from disruption of normal hydrogen peroxide-producing lactobacilli.
additionalInvestigations: Nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) for Chlamydia and Gonorrhoea
Transvaginal pelvic ultrasound to exclude tubo-ovarian abscess
Saline wet mount and 10% KOH amine whiff test with vaginal pH measurement
